18: # Goal Set-String Playbook
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: A packet's goal document can be as long as it needs to be. The objective an operator sets cannot: every runtime goal surface caps what it holds, and a slice that will not fit is truncated at the tail, which is exactly where the completion criteria live.
25: 
26: Goal authoring belongs to `sk-create-goal`, run through `/create:goal`. Its [budget-and-handoff.md](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/budget-and-handoff.md) holds the budget, the one cut order and what a parent goal sent in chat contains, and its [parent-and-nested-goals.md](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/parent-and-nested-goals.md) holds precedence and amendments. This playbook covers what system-spec-kit owns: the set string a runtime binds and when a changed goal is resent.
27: 
28: This playbook fixes the shape of what gets typed. The rule it complements checks the file: a phase parent or top-level `goal.md` has one limit, 4,000 durable characters, measured from the frontmatter's closing fence to the log anchor. Up to 4,000 passes and past it fails. Nothing can check what an operator pastes, so the shape below is guidance rather than a gate.
29: 
30: ---
31: 
32: ## 2. THE SHAPE
33: 
34: ```text
35: Execute specs/<track>/<packet>/goal.md.
36: 
37: BINDING: read each phase's goal.md before working that phase; its criteria bind
38: as if written here. PRECEDENCE: parent decisions outrank child detail; child
39: detail outranks any summary of it.
40: 
41: DONE WHEN:
42: - <criterion copied verbatim from the packet's goal document>
43: - <criterion>
44: - <criterion>
45: ```
46: 
47: Three parts, in this order:
48: 
49: 1. **The pointer.** One line naming the packet's goal document. Roughly 60 characters.
50: 2. **The binding and precedence sentence.** Two sentences that turn the reference into an obligation. Without them the pointer is a citation, and a citation gets skimmed.
51: 3. **The completion criteria, copied.** Not referenced. Copied.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## 3. WHY THE CRITERIA ARE COPIED
56: 
57: Nothing dereferences a path inside an objective string. Every goal surface in this repository is string-in, string-out: the working agent can open the file because it has tools, but whatever judges completion sees only the stored string.
58: 
59: Leave the criteria in the file alone and the evaluator is judging a table of contents. Copy them and it can judge the packet. This is the one duplication the design accepts. The rules for writing criteria that survive the copy are section 4 of `sk-create-goal`'s [authoring-standards.md](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/authoring-standards.md).
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: ## 4. WHEN IT WILL NOT FIT
64: 
65: The validator fails a parent past 4,000 durable characters. That is the one limit, with no warning tier below it, so a parent under 4,000 needs no cutting. Which goals carry it is section 2 of [budget-and-handoff.md](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/budget-and-handoff.md): a child is unbounded unless it is itself a phase parent. When a parent is over, cut it in the order section 3 of [budget-and-handoff.md](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/budget-and-handoff.md) gives, which is the one full cut order.
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 5. RESENDING THE PARENT GOAL
70: 
71: The objective the operator set is a copy of the parent goal, and copies drift.
72: The goal document is the source, so the agent working the packet owns the resync:
73: 
74: 1. Whenever anything above the log changes (the objective, a decision, the
75:    binding table, a criterion), resend the parent's `chat_slice`, unprompted,
76:    so the operator can paste it over the session objective. On Claude Code,
77:    send it as one fenced code block that holds the slice and nothing else.
78:    `node .skilled/hooks/goal/bin/goal.cjs packet <packet> --workspace <repo root>`
79:    prints it, JSON-quoted. What that slice contains, and the `packet_budget=ok`
80:    check before it is sent, are section 4 of [budget-and-handoff.md](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/budget-and-handoff.md). It
81:    is a different payload from the Section 2 shape, which is what a runtime
82:    stores when it binds the packet. Keep reminding while it stays unset. Never
83:    stop work because it is unset: only the operator stops work. After the
84:    operator sets it, acknowledge in one line and continue.
85: 2. A child `goal.md` change that alters a parent decision or criterion is a
86:    parent amendment, handled as section 6 of
87:    [parent-and-nested-goals.md](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/parent-and-nested-goals.md) says. A child change that stays inside
88:    its own phase needs no resend.
89: 3. Log entries never trigger a resend, because the log is not part of the objective.
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 6. CREATING THE FILE
94: 
95: Nothing writes `goal.md` unasked. Two paths exist:
96: 
97: 1. `create.sh ... --with-goal` scaffolds it with the other packet documents.
98:    With `--phase` it writes a `goal.md` into each new child only.
99:    `--level phase-parent --with-goal` writes a parent goal.
100: 2. `/create:goal <packet> <operation>` authors any goal from `sk-create-goal`'s
101:    per-kind templates: `phase-parent` for a parent, `phase-add` or `child` for
102:    a new phase, `amend` for a change and `retrofit` for a packet that has none.
103: 
104: The `goal.md` in a packet and the session objective an operator sets with the
105: goal command are two different things that share a word. The document is the
106: source: it lives in the packet, carries the durable slice and the log, and is
107: what this playbook describes. The session objective is a string the runtime
108: holds for the current session and judges completion against. Nothing copies
109: one into the other. The resync rule in Section 5 is the bridge, and the
110: operator's hands carry it.
111: 
112: ---
113: 
114: ## 7. WORKED EXAMPLE
115: 
116: From a real four-phase packet whose durable slice measures 1,986 characters, well under the 4,000 limit:
117: 
118: ```text
119: Execute specs/system-speckit/031-system-speckit-v4/010-goal-file-addon/goal.md.
120: 
121: BINDING: read each phase's goal.md before working that phase; its criteria bind
122: as if written here. PRECEDENCE: parent decisions outrank child detail; child
123: detail outranks any summary of it.
124: 
125: DONE WHEN:
126: - validate.sh --strict recursive over this packet exits 0
127: - Every phase reports its acceptance criteria closeable
128: - The document resolves to a template at 1/2/3/3+/phase and to nothing at review
129: - A packet with no goal document validates exactly as before
130: ```
131: 
132: That set string is 529 characters. The packet's goal document is 4,243. The
133: difference is what the pointer buys.
134: 
135: ---
136: 
137: ## 8. RELATED
138: 
139: | Document | Role |
140: |---|---|
141: | [validation-rules.md](../validation/validation-rules.md) | `SPEC_DOC_SUFFICIENCY`, whose goal diagnostics check the durable budget and the binding table |
142: | [quick-reference.md](./quick-reference.md) | First-touch command surface |
143: | [budget-and-handoff.md](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/budget-and-handoff.md) | `sk-create-goal`: the budget, the one cut order and what a parent goal sent in chat contains |
144: | [parent-and-nested-goals.md](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-goal/references/parent-and-nested-goals.md) | `sk-create-goal`: parent, child, phase-add and retrofit authoring, precedence and amendments |

13: 
14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```
335: 
336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead
340: 
341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown
347: ### [Pattern Name]
348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]
350: \```[language]
351: // Bad code with issues
352: // Showing what NOT to do
353: \```
354: 
355: **AFTER**: [Solution description]
356: \```[language]
357: // Good code with fixes
358: // Showing correct approach
359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale
369: 
370: ### Pattern Comparison Tables
371: 
372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
373: 
374: **Format**:
375: ```markdown
376: ### Common Patterns
377: 
378: | Scenario     | Approach A (Wrong) | Approach B (Right) | Why Better  |
379: | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
380: | [Scenario 1] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison
385: 
386: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
387: 
388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
389: 
390: **Format**:
391: \```markdown
392: ### Decision Logic
393: 
394: \```markdown
395: IF [condition A]:
396:   → [Action/Path A]
397:   → [Expected outcome A]
398: 
399: IF [condition B]:
400:   → [Action/Path B]
401:   → [Expected outcome B]
402: 
403: IF [condition C]:
404:   → [Action/Path C]

411: \```
412: Analyze situation

414: │  └─ Execute Workflow A
415: │     └─ Expected outcome A

417: │  └─ Execute Workflow B
418: │     └─ Expected outcome B

424:

426: 
427: **Purpose**: Named checkpoints throughout workflows

429: **Format**:

433:

440: **Usage**: Reference in quality checklists and debugging

452: [1-2 sentence summary only - no prerequisites here]

501: \```

503: **Format for Scripts**:

506: ```

513: ### Common Error Patterns
514: 
515: **Purpose**: Document actual errors with explanations
516: 
517: **Format**:

520:

525: 
526: // [Another error message]
527: // → [What it means]
528: // → [How to fix]
529: \```
530: \```
531: 
532: **Example**:
533: \```markdown

535: 
536: \```javascript
537: // Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'X' of undefined
538: // → Variable is undefined, check initialization
539: // → Verify element exists before accessing properties
540: 
541: // Failed to load resource: net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT
542: // → Ad blocker or browser extension blocking resource

545: \```

548: 
549: **Purpose**: Explicitly state what's in/out of scope

551: **Format**:

554: 
555: **Out of scope:** [What is NOT supported]

583: 
584: ### Phased Workflow with Checkpoints Example
585: 
586: **Purpose**: Show complete workflow with validation gates

652: 
653: **Actions**:
654: 1. Read user request carefully
655: 2. Identify affected files and systems
656: 3. Review relevant documentation
657: 
658: **Validation**: `requirements_understood`
659: - Can I clearly explain what needs to be done?
660: - Do I know which files will change?
661: - Are there any unclear requirements?
662: 
663: #### Phase 2: Design
664: 
665: **Purpose**: Plan the implementation approach
666: 
667: **Actions**:
668: 1. Choose simplest solution that works
669: 2. Identify potential edge cases
670: 3. Plan validation strategy
671: 
672: **Validation**: `design_approved`
673: - Is this the simplest approach?
674: - Have I considered edge cases?
675: - Can I test this effectively?
676: 
677: [Continue with remaining phases...]
678: ```
679: 
680: ---
681: 
682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

14: # Nested Changelog Workflow
15: 
16: > **Deprecated.** Spec folders no longer get changelogs. `/speckit:implement` and `/speckit:complete` no longer write one, and `/create:changelog` writes only to `.skilled/changelog/`. The generator stays and prints a deprecation notice on stderr, so the existing packet changelogs can still be rendered. Those files stay and still validate. The rest of this page is reference for them and for the generator, not an instruction to write new ones.
17: 
18: Packet-local changelogs captured completion state inside a spec folder instead of the global `.skilled/changelog/` release stream.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: Re-render the existing packet-local changelog files for spec roots and phase child folders.
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## 2. WHEN TO USE
29: 
30: Do not use it for new work. Write new changelog entries with `/create:changelog`, which writes to `.skilled/changelog/`.
31: 
32: - Re-render an existing packet changelog under `specs/**/changelog/` after its packet docs changed. The generator refuses a packet that has no changelog
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## 3. GENERATOR
37: 
38: ```bash
39: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/spec-folder/nested-changelog.js <spec-folder> --write
40: ```
41: 
42: `--write` re-renders a changelog that already exists. When the resolved output file is missing it exits with an error that points at `/create:changelog` and writes nothing.
43: 
44: ### Modes
45: 
46: | Mode | Detected when | Output |
47: |---|---|---|
48: | `root` | The target folder is a spec root | `<spec-folder>/changelog/changelog-<packet>-root.md` |
49: | `phase` | The target folder is a direct phase child | `<parent-spec>/changelog/changelog-<packet>-<phase-folder>.md` |
50: 
51: ### Search Metadata
52: 
53: Each rendered changelog carries one identity phrase in `trigger_phrases`, so a lookup by packet and phase name finds it. The generator derives the phrase from the output path:
54: 
55: 1. Take the filename stem, drop `changelog-` and up to three leading number groups, then drop a trailing `root`.
56: 2. Take the owner: the folder that holds `changelog/`, or the parent folder when the file sits deeper inside a changelog tree. Drop its number groups too.
57: 3. Write the owner's words, then the entry's words. Where the owner's last words repeat the entry's first words, write them once.
58: 4. Past nine words, trim the owner from its end. The entry's own words always survive whole.
59: 5. End with `changelog` unless the words already end with it.
60: 
61: A packet folder `042-search-overhaul` gets `search overhaul changelog` for its root changelog and `search overhaul ranking fix changelog` for its `003-ranking-fix` phase. Both templates carry the phrase as the `{{CHANGELOG_IDENTITY_PHRASE}}` placeholder rather than a fixed phrase, because a fixed phrase in a template names every packet's changelog at once.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 4. EVIDENCE STACK
66: 
67: The generator prefers these sources, in order:
68: 
69: 1. `implementation-summary.md`
70: 2. `tasks.md`
71: 3. `checklist.md` (root mode only, when a legacy packet still has one)
72: 4. `spec.md`
73: 
74: It does not read `acceptance-criteria.md` or `decision-record.md`. It derives summary, change bullets, verification notes, files changed and follow-ups from the available packet evidence. Root changelogs also roll up direct child phase folders when they exist.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 5. CANONICAL TEMPLATES
79: 
80: - `templates/changelog/root.md`
81: - `templates/changelog/phase.md`
82: 
83: The deprecated generator renders existing packet changelogs from these templates. Do not reuse the global `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md` for nested packet output.
84: 
85: ---

16: # Intake Contract Reference
17: 
18: This reference module defines the single canonical intake contract used by any SpecKit command that needs to create, repair, or resume a spec folder. Callers execute this contract inline rather than invoking a separate command — the workflow runs as Step 1 of `/speckit:plan` and Section 0 of `/speckit:complete`.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Define the canonical spec-folder intake contract shared by `/speckit:plan`, `/speckit:complete`, and `/speckit:resume` re-entry.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: Load this reference when a command needs to classify, create, repair, resume, or publish the canonical spec-folder trio.
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: All intake surfaces return the same `start_state`, `repair_mode`, relationship data, and trio-publication semantics, even when the caller owns the visible prompt.
35: 
36: ### Source Marker
37: 
38: <!-- SPECKIT_REFERENCE_SOURCE: intake-contract | v1.0 -->
39: `/speckit:plan --intake-only` exposes intake as a standalone surface (halts after the Emit phase); `/speckit:resume` redirects re-entry for `reentry_reason in {incomplete-interview, placeholder-upgrade, metadata-repair}` to `/speckit:plan --intake-only` with prefilled state.
40: 
41: ### Contract Interface
42: 
43: **Inputs** (resolved by caller before entering the intake workflow):
44: - `$ARGUMENTS` — optional feature description plus pre-binding flags
45: - `--spec-folder=PATH` — explicit target (bypass auto-discovery)
46: - `--level=N` — pre-set documentation level (1 / 2 / 3 / 3+)
47: - `--start-state=STATE` — pre-classified folder state
48: - `--repair-mode=MODE` — pre-selected repair mode
49: - `--record-relationships=yes|no` — relationship-capture toggle
50: - `--depends-on=PACKET_ID[,PACKET_ID...]` — seed depends_on
51: - `--related-to=PACKET_ID[,PACKET_ID...]` — seed related_to
52: - `--supersedes=PACKET_ID[,PACKET_ID...]` — seed supersedes
53: - `--intake-only` — (plan.md only) halt after Emit phase
54: 
55: > **Phase parent note.** When the invoking workflow targets a folder that already qualifies as a phase parent (≥1 NNN-named populated child), level selection and Level extension composition do not apply at the parent level. The intake publishes only the lean trio (`spec.md` + `description.json` + `graph-metadata.json`) using `templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl` as the parent scaffold. Heavy docs live in the children. Phase children created alongside the parent still go through the full Level 1–3+ contract for their assigned level.
56: 
57: **Outputs** (returned to caller, or surfaced alongside caller-local preflight state when the invoking workflow emits both):
58: - `feature_description` — free-text description
59: - `spec_path` — resolved target folder path
60: - `folder_state` — caller-local Step 0 classifier used by the invoking YAML asset (`no-spec | partial-folder | repair-mode | placeholder-upgrade | populated-folder`); surface for diagnostics and event parity only
61: - `start_state` — canonical intake-contract state mapped from `folder_state` and consumed downstream (see §3)
62: - `repair_mode` — selected mode (see §4)
63: - `execution_mode` — AUTONOMOUS | INTERACTIVE
64: - `level_recommendation` — output of `recommend-level.sh`
65: - `selected_level` — kept recommendation or user override
66: - `manual_relationships` — `{ depends_on, related_to, supersedes }` grouped with packet_id dedup
67: - `resume_question_id` — first unresolved question ID or null
68: - `reentry_reason` — `none | incomplete-interview | placeholder-upgrade | metadata-repair`
69: - `STATUS` — `OK | FAIL | CANCELLED`
70: 
71: ---
72: 
73: ## 2. WORKFLOW PHASES
74: 
75: | Phase | Purpose | Outputs |
76: |-------|---------|---------|
77: | Preflight | Inspect + classify folder; acquire advisory intake lock | `spec_path`, `folder_state` (caller-local), `start_state` (canonical), `repair_mode`, `resume_question_id`, `reentry_reason` |
78: | Interview | Consolidated single-prompt Q0–Q4+ for missing fields | `feature_description`, `level_recommendation`, `selected_level`, `manual_relationships` |
79: | Emit | Stage + rename canonical trio (`spec.md`, `description.json`, `graph-metadata.json`) | Canonical trio published or fail-closed recovery output |
80: | Save | Optional memory-save branch (only when structured context exists) | Independent memory-save result |
81: | Report | Return stable contract to caller | `STATUS=OK\|FAIL\|CANCELLED` with all returned fields |
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## 3. FOLDER STATE CLASSIFICATION
86: 
87: Invoking YAML assets first classify a local `folder_state`, then map it to the canonical `start_state` enum before returning contract outputs or emitting intake events. After T-YML-PLN-01, four of the five tokens align 1:1; only the empty-folder case keeps a local-vs-canonical rename.
88: 
89: | Local `folder_state` | Canonical `start_state` | Consumption |
90: |----------------------|-------------------------|-------------|
91: | `no-spec` | `empty-folder` | Local branch token only; downstream callers should consume `start_state=empty-folder` |
92: | `partial-folder` | `partial-folder` | Shared across local branching and canonical intake contract |
93: | `repair-mode` | `repair-mode` | Shared across local branching and canonical intake contract |
94: | `placeholder-upgrade` | `placeholder-upgrade` | Shared across local branching and canonical intake contract |
95: | `populated-folder` | `populated-folder` | Shared across local branching and canonical intake contract |
96: 
97: The canonical `start_state` values are:
98: 
99: | State | Detection | Default repair_mode |
100: |-------|-----------|---------------------|
101: | `empty-folder` | Folder missing OR no `spec.md`, no `description.json`, no `graph-metadata.json`, no tracked seed markers | `create` |
102: | `partial-folder` | Folder exists, trio incomplete, no tracked seed markers, no intake lock | `repair-metadata` |
103: | `repair-mode` | Folder exists, trio present but metadata invalid (schema failure, missing required fields) | `repair-metadata` |
104: | `placeholder-upgrade` | Tracked seed markers present (e.g., `[###-feature-name]`, `[YYYY-MM-DD]` in non-placeholder positions) | `resolve-placeholders` |
105: | `populated-folder` | Full trio present, metadata valid, no seed markers | `abort` (unless user explicitly opts into repair/overwrite) |
106: 
107: **Tracked seed markers** force `placeholder-upgrade` even when a folder otherwise looks populated. Tracked markers include:
108: - `[###-feature-name]` in `implementation-summary.md` metadata when the packet is supposed to be closed
109: - `[YYYY-MM-DD]` in verification dates
110: - Template-placeholder fragments left unfilled
111: 
112: > **Note:** `implementation-summary.md` with `[###-feature-name]` during the *planning* phase is NOT a tracked marker — it is the expected placeholder until implementation completes. Classification must distinguish planning-phase placeholders from closeout-phase placeholders.
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## 4. REPAIR-MODE ROUTING
117: 
118: After folder classification, the caller confirms (or overrides) the repair mode before the Interview phase runs:
119: 
120: | Mode | Purpose | Behavior |
121: |------|---------|----------|
122: | `create` | Fresh spec folder | Author canonical trio from scratch; run full interview |
123: | `repair-metadata` | Fix broken `description.json` / `graph-metadata.json` / partial trio | Re-run helpers (`generate-description.js`, graph backfill) without overwriting `spec.md` body |
124: | `resolve-placeholders` | Fill tracked seed markers | Interview only for unresolved markers; other canonical content preserved |
125: | `abort` | Populated folder, no repair intent | Return STATUS=CANCELLED, no mutations |
126: 
127: `abort` is the default for `populated-folder` unless the caller explicitly selects a repair path. Never auto-overwrite a populated folder.
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ## 5. CONSOLIDATED INTERVIEW
132: 
133: All missing inputs are gathered in a SINGLE consolidated prompt. Never split into multiple messages.
134: 
135: **Questions** (asked only if unresolved by flags or discovery):
136: 
137: - **Q0. Feature Description** — what the spec folder captures
138: - **Q1. Target Folder State** — A) empty/create · B) partial/resume · C) repair metadata · D) populated/review
139: - **Q2. Documentation Level** — recommendation from `recommend-level.sh`; keep or override to Level 1 / 2 / 3 / 3+
140: - **Q3. Record Relationships Now?** — A) No · B) Yes
141: - **Q4+. Relationship Entries** (only if Q3 = Yes) — grouped `depends_on`, `related_to`, `supersedes` with `packet_id` key and dedup per relation type
142: 
143: **Reply format examples:**
144: - `"Feature intake refactor, A, keep, A"`
145: - `"B, override to Level 3, B, depends_on=026-009 reason: build on prior graph audit"`
146: 
147: Parse the response into the returned contract fields. In `:auto` mode, proceed only when the full contract is pre-bound by args or inherited parent state; otherwise the ASK path still applies.
148: 
149: ---
150: 
151: ## 6. CANONICAL TRIO PUBLICATION
152: 
153: The Emit phase stages and commits three files atomically:
154: 
155: 1. `spec.md` — canonical specification (per Level 1 / 2 / 3 / 3+ template)
156: 2. `description.json` — generated via `node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/spec-folder/generate-description.js <folder> <base>`
157: 3. `graph-metadata.json` — generated via backfill or authored with supersedes/depends_on from `manual_relationships`
158: 
159: **Staged semantics:**
160: - Write to `<file>.tmp` first
161: - After all three temp writes succeed, rename atomically
162: - On any failure mid-write: remove temp files, preserve pre-existing files, emit exact recovery command
163: - Helper: `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh` for full trio generation
164: 
165: **Success condition:** All three canonical files present and structurally valid BEFORE the optional memory-save branch runs. The save branch is never the success gate.
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## 7. MANUAL RELATIONSHIPS
170: 
171: Relationship objects use:
172: ```json
173: {
174:   "packet_id": "project-track/NNN-slug",
175:   "reason": "one-sentence justification",
176:   "source": "spec.md:Scope",
177:   "spec_folder": "optional-override-path",
178:   "title": "optional-human-title"
179: }
180: ```
181: 
182: **Dedup rule:** within each relation type (`depends_on`, `related_to`, `supersedes`), entries dedupe by `packet_id`. Last entry wins.
183: 
184: **Storage:** persisted in `graph-metadata.json` under `manual.depends_on[]`, `manual.related_to[]`, `manual.supersedes[]`.
185: 
186: ---
187: 
188: ## 8. RESUME SEMANTICS
189: 
190: When a session is interrupted mid-intake, `resume_question_id` and `reentry_reason` persist the re-entry point.
191: 
192: | reentry_reason | Meaning | Re-entry path |
193: |----------------|---------|---------------|
194: | `none` | Clean state | Not a re-entry |
195: | `incomplete-interview` | User abandoned mid-prompt | `/speckit:plan --intake-only` with prefilled state |
196: | `placeholder-upgrade` | Seed marker resolution was pending | `/speckit:plan --intake-only` with `--repair-mode=resolve-placeholders` |
197: | `metadata-repair` | Trio schema validation failed | `/speckit:plan --intake-only` with `--repair-mode=repair-metadata` |
198: 
199: `/speckit:resume` reads these fields from handover state and routes accordingly.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 9. INTAKE LOCK
204: 
205: An advisory lock file prevents concurrent trio publication on the same folder.
206: 
207: **Scope:** Step 1 (intake) only. Release on Emit success OR on cancel/abort. Do NOT hold the lock across planning Steps 2–8 of `/speckit:plan`.
208: 
209: **Fail-closed behavior:**
210: - Stale lock (older than a conservative timeout): surface exact cleanup command (`rm <path>.intake.lock`)
211: - Contended lock (another session active): fail with guidance to retry after that session reports STATUS
212: - Never silently take an existing lock
213: 
214: ---
215: 
216: ## 10. OPTIONAL MEMORY SAVE BRANCH
217: 
218: Memory save runs AFTER Emit success, only when:
219: - Structured context exists beyond the canonical trio (e.g., research artifacts, decision records, prior session handoffs)
220: - Caller explicitly allows the branch (default: skip for fresh creates, allow for repair/resume)
221: 
222: Invocation:
223: ```bash
224: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js /tmp/save-context-data-<session-id>.json specs/007-feature/
225: ```
226: 
227: Report save result independently from trio success — a failed save never invalidates a successful trio.
228: 
229: ---
230: 
231: ## 11. ERROR HANDLING
232: 
233: | Error | Action |
234: |-------|--------|
235: | Populated folder without explicit repair approval | Abort with STATUS=CANCELLED; show repair/overwrite choices |
236: | Stale or contended intake lock | Fail closed (STATUS=FAIL) with exact cleanup or retry guidance |
237: | Missing template or helper failure | Halt Emit; preserve pre-existing files; report failing helper |
238: | Tracked seed-marker conflict | Reclassify to `placeholder-upgrade` OR halt on ambiguity |
239: | Memory save requested without structured context | Skip save branch; keep canonical trio as success |
240: | Staged rename failure | Remove temp files; keep pre-existing files; STATUS=FAIL |
241: 
242: ---
243: 
244: ## 12. CONSUMER INTEGRATION
245: 
246: ### `/speckit:plan`
247: 
248: Step 1 (Intake) references this module. Plan's consolidated setup prompt (Section 0) detects folder state early:
249: 
250: - `populated-folder` + no `--intake-only` → skip intake block; proceed to Step 2 (Request Analysis)
251: - `populated-folder` + `--intake-only` → no-op exit with informational message
252: - Any non-`populated` state → execute Phases 1–5 of this contract, then proceed OR halt if `--intake-only`
253: 
254: ### `/speckit:complete`
255: 
256: Section 0 references this module with identical semantics:
257: 
258: - `populated-folder` → skip intake; proceed to plan + implement + verify pipeline
259: - Any non-`populated` state → execute Phases 1–5, then proceed through full completion workflow
260: 
261: ### `/speckit:resume`
262: 
263: Reads `handover.md` and `_memory.continuity` for `reentry_reason` and `resume_question_id`. Routes intake re-entry to `/speckit:plan --intake-only` with appropriate `--repair-mode` and `--start-state` prefilled from saved state.
264: 
265: ---
266: 
267: ## 13. QUALITY GATES
268: 
269: - Folder state classified to exactly one of the five values
270: - `level_recommendation` and `selected_level` stored separately (override never erases recommendation)
271: - Manual relationships dedupe by `packet_id` within each relation type
272: - Canonical trio published via staged temp + rename; pre-existing files intact on failure
273: - Intake lock acquired at Phase 1 entry, released at Phase 3 exit (or on cancel)
274: - `:confirm` mode pauses at four gates: folder-state review, interview summary, canonical trio emission, optional save branching
275: - `:auto` mode reaches zero prompts only when the full contract is pre-bound
276: 
277: ---
278: 
279: ## 14. REFERENCE
280: 
281: | Category | Paths |
282: |----------|-------|
283: | Spec-kit templates | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/` (Level 1 / 2 / 3 / 3+) |
284: | Phase-parent template | `templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl` (lean trio template) |
285: | Recommend-level helper | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh` |
286: | Create helper | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh` |
287: | Description generator | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/spec-folder/generate-description.js` |
288: | Memory save script | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js` |
289: | Validator | `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <folder> --strict` |
290: | Deep-research spec check | `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/references/protocol/spec-check-protocol.md` |
291: 
292: ---
293: 
294: ## 15. SUPERSEDES
295: 
296: This module supersedes the deleted standalone intake command surface that packet `012-command-graph-consolidation` removed from `026-graph-and-context-optimization`. The former standalone intake surface duplicated the same logic that `/speckit:plan` and `/speckit:complete` carried inline, producing three parallel copies that drifted independently. Consolidation into this single reference eliminates drift risk and simplifies the command graph.
297: 
298: **Packet reference:** internal design notes
299: 
300: **Delivery note:** The implementation delivered 15 milestones (M1-M9 on 2026-04-14, M10-M15 on 2026-04-15). `/speckit:plan` and `/speckit:complete` reference this module in place of inline intake blocks; `/speckit:plan --intake-only` provides the standalone invocation path with an explicit YAML gate. See the local decision record for the architectural rationale (ADR-002 through ADR-010).
301: 
302: ---

124: | `resolve-placeholders` | Fill tracked seed markers | Interview only for unresolved markers; other canonical content preserved |
125: | `abort` | Populated folder, no repair intent | Return STATUS=CANCELLED, no mutations |
126: 
127: `abort` is the default for `populated-folder` unless the caller explicitly selects a repair path. Never auto-overwrite a populated folder.
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ## 5. CONSOLIDATED INTERVIEW
132: 
133: All missing inputs are gathered in a SINGLE consolidated prompt. Never split into multiple messages.
134: 
135: **Questions** (asked only if unresolved by flags or discovery):
136: 
137: - **Q0. Feature Description** — what the spec folder captures
138: - **Q1. Target Folder State** — A) empty/create · B) partial/resume · C) repair metadata · D) populated/review
139: - **Q2. Documentation Level** — recommendation from `recommend-level.sh`; keep or override to Level 1 / 2 / 3 / 3+
140: - **Q3. Record Relationships Now?** — A) No · B) Yes
141: - **Q4+. Relationship Entries** (only if Q3 = Yes) — grouped `depends_on`, `related_to`, `supersedes` with `packet_id` key and dedup per relation type
142: 
143: **Reply format examples:**
144: - `"Feature intake refactor, A, keep, A"`
145: - `"B, override to Level 3, B, depends_on=026-009 reason: build on prior graph audit"`
146: 
147: Parse the response into the returned contract fields. In `:auto` mode, proceed only when the full contract is pre-bound by args or inherited parent state; otherwise the ASK path still applies.
148:
