151: ## 6. CANONICAL TRIO PUBLICATION
152: 
153: The Emit phase stages and commits three files atomically:
154: 
155: 1. `spec.md` — canonical specification (per Level 1 / 2 / 3 / 3+ template)
156: 2. `description.json` — generated via `node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/spec-folder/generate-description.js <folder> <base>`
157: 3. `graph-metadata.json` — generated via backfill or authored with supersedes/depends_on from `manual_relationships`
158: 
159: **Staged semantics:**
160: - Write to `<file>.tmp` first
161: - After all three temp writes succeed, rename atomically
162: - On any failure mid-write: remove temp files, preserve pre-existing files, emit exact recovery command
163: - Helper: `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh` for full trio generation
164: 
165: **Success condition:** All three canonical files present and structurally valid BEFORE the optional memory-save branch runs. The save branch is never the success gate.
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## 7. MANUAL RELATIONSHIPS
170: 
171: Relationship objects use:
172: ```json
173: {
174:   "packet_id": "project-track/NNN-slug",
175:   "reason": "one-sentence justification",
176:   "source": "spec.md:Scope",
177:   "spec_folder": "optional-override-path",
178:   "title": "optional-human-title"
179: }
180: ```
181: 
182: **Dedup rule:** within each relation type (`depends_on`, `related_to`, `supersedes`), entries dedupe by `packet_id`. Last entry wins.
183: 
184: **Storage:** persisted in `graph-metadata.json` under `manual.depends_on[]`, `manual.related_to[]`, `manual.supersedes[]`.
185: 
186: ---

188: ## 8. RESUME SEMANTICS
189: 
190: When a session is interrupted mid-intake, `resume_question_id` and `reentry_reason` persist the re-entry point.
191: 
192: | reentry_reason | Meaning | Re-entry path |
193: |----------------|---------|---------------|
194: | `none` | Clean state | Not a re-entry |
195: | `incomplete-interview` | User abandoned mid-prompt | `/speckit:plan --intake-only` with prefilled state |
196: | `placeholder-upgrade` | Seed marker resolution was pending | `/speckit:plan --intake-only` with `--repair-mode=resolve-placeholders` |
197: | `metadata-repair` | Trio schema validation failed | `/speckit:plan --intake-only` with `--repair-mode=repair-metadata` |
198: 
199: `/speckit:resume` reads these fields from handover state and routes accordingly.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 9. INTAKE LOCK
204: 
205: An advisory lock file prevents concurrent trio publication on the same folder.
206: 
207: **Scope:** Step 1 (intake) only. Release on Emit success OR on cancel/abort. Do NOT hold the lock across planning Steps 2–8 of `/speckit:plan`.
208: 
209: **Fail-closed behavior:**
210: - Stale lock (older than a conservative timeout): surface exact cleanup command (`rm <path>.intake.lock`)
211: - Contended lock (another session active): fail with guidance to retry after that session reports STATUS
212: - Never silently take an existing lock
213: 
214: ---

216: ## 10. OPTIONAL MEMORY SAVE BRANCH
217: 
218: Memory save runs AFTER Emit success, only when:
219: - Structured context exists beyond the canonical trio (e.g., research artifacts, decision records, prior session handoffs)
220: - Caller explicitly allows the branch (default: skip for fresh creates, allow for repair/resume)

222: Invocation:

225: ```
226: 
227: Report save result independently from trio success — a failed save never invalidates a successful trio.
228: 
229: ---

231: ## 11. ERROR HANDLING
232: 
233: | Error | Action |
234: |-------|--------|
235: | Populated folder without explicit repair approval | Abort with STATUS=CANCELLED; show repair/overwrite choices |
236: | Stale or contended intake lock | Fail closed (STATUS=FAIL) with exact cleanup or retry guidance |
237: | Missing template or helper failure | Halt Emit; preserve pre-existing files; report failing helper |
238: | Tracked seed-marker conflict | Reclassify to `placeholder-upgrade` OR halt on ambiguity |
239: | Memory save requested without structured context | Skip save branch; keep canonical trio as success |
240: | Staged rename failure | Remove temp files; keep pre-existing files; STATUS=FAIL |

245: 
246: ### `/speckit:plan`
247: 
248: Step 1 (Intake) references this module. Plan's consolidated setup prompt (Section 0) detects folder state early:
249:

261: ### `/speckit:resume`
262: 
263: Reads `handover.md` and `_memory.continuity` for `reentry_reason` and `resume_question_id`. Routes intake re-entry to `/speckit:plan --intake-only` with appropriate `--repair-mode` and `--start-state` prefilled from saved state.

267: ## 13. QUALITY GATES
268: 
269: - Folder state classified to exactly one of the five values
270: - `level_recommendation` and `selected_level` stored separately (override never erases recommendation)
271: - Manual relationships dedupe by `packet_id` within each relation type

343: ### "Can I change levels mid-work?"
344: 
345: **Yes:**
346: - Going up: Add additional files (see Level Migration table)
347: - Going down: Keep existing docs (uncommon)

354: **Rule:**

356: - Once you write/edit ANY files = SPEC REQUIRED

362:

367: - ✅ Documentation files (*.md, *.txt, docs/)
368: - ✅ Configuration files (*.json, *.yaml, *.toml)
369: - ✅ Knowledge base files

371: - ✅ Build files (package.json, requirements.txt)

375: - ❌ Whitespace-only changes

382: **Create `decision-record-*.md` when making:**

465: ## 15. CONTEXT SAVE & HANDOVER
466: 
467: ### Context Save
468: 
469: **Manual triggers (OpenCode):**
470: - Command: `/speckit:save`
471: - Keywords: "save context", "save conversation", "save this"
472: 
473: **Note:** OpenCode does not support automatic interval-based saves (hooks are event-triggered via plugins, not time-interval).
474: 
475: **MANDATORY:** Use generate-context.js for memory save:
476: ```
477: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js /tmp/save-context-data-<session-id>.json specs/###-folder/
478: ```
479: 
480: Use `generate-context.js` for routine metadata and index saves. Quick direct edits are allowed only for `_memory.continuity` YAML frontmatter blocks in `implementation-summary.md`.
481: 
482: > **Recovery Integration:** Packet recovery is canonical-first. Start from `handover.md`, then `_memory.continuity` in `implementation-summary.md`, then the rest of the packet docs before widening with a ripgrep sweep over the specs tree.
483: 
484: **Phased Resume**: When the target folder has child phases, first resolve
485: whether you need the coordination root or an active child.
486: Load/save memory in the child packet by default.
487: Only load root memory when updating coordination snapshots.
488: 
489: **Phase-Parent Resume Ladder**: When the resume target is a phase parent (folder has `[0-9]{3}-name/` children with `spec.md` or `description.json`), `/speckit:resume` honors the pointer first:
490: 
491: 1. Read the pointer, from the telemetry store first and then from `derived.last_active_child_id` in the parent's `graph-metadata.json`. When it names an existing child packet inside the parent, recurse into that child at any age, report the child and its `derived.last_active_at`, and apply the child's normal handover → `_memory.continuity` → spec docs ladder. Confirm mode asks first when the pointer is older than 24 hours.
492: 2. If the pointer is null, missing, malformed, points outside the parent, or names a child that no longer exists, fall back to listing children with statuses (sourced from each child's `graph-metadata.json` `derived.status`) and let the user pick.
493: 3. `--no-redirect` flag bypasses the pointer step entirely and shows the parent's spec.md plus child list.
494: 
495: The pointer is maintained automatically by the generator: a save into a child points every phase-parent ancestor one level down toward it. A save aimed at a phase parent moves the pointers only when a `--full-auto` save routes its continuity into a leaf, and otherwise moves none. A track root keeps its pointer in the telemetry store only. Atomic write via temp+rename. No `_memory.continuity` block exists at a phase parent (per the lean trio policy — parents have no `implementation-summary.md`).
496: 
497: **Save location:**
498: - Primary: the active packet's canonical continuity surfaces
499: - Core continuity block: `_memory.continuity` in `implementation-summary.md`
500: - No workspace-root fallback; direct CLI targets stay inside the selected root spec or phase packet
501: 
502: ### Session Continuity Save
503: 
504: **Command:** `/speckit:save`
505: 
506: **Purpose:** Refresh packet continuity before a pause or handoff while keeping `handover.md`, `_memory.continuity`, and the packet docs aligned for the next `/speckit:resume` pass.
507: 
508: **Use when:**
509: - Ending a long session
510: - Context compaction detected
511: - Handing off to another session
512: - Before complex multi-step operations
513:

516: ## 16. PHASE WORKFLOW SHORTCUTS
517: 
518: ### Phase Commands
519: 
520: | Command | Description |
521: |---------|-------------|
522: | `/speckit:plan :with-phases` | Trigger phase decomposition as pre-workflow in plan or complete |
523: | `create.sh --phase --phases N --phase-names a,b,c <description>` | Create a phase parent and named child phase folders |
524: | `create.sh --phase --parent <parent> --phases N --phase-names a,b <description>` | Add named child phases to an existing parent spec |
525: | `validate.sh <parent> --recursive` | Validate parent and all child phase folders |
526: 
527: ### Phase Quick Reference
528: 
529: **Detection:** Complexity score >= 25 AND level >= 3, or a series parent for a different change to the same artifact
530: 
531: **Scoring dimensions:** Architectural (10) + Files>15 (10) + LOC>800 (10) + Risk>=2 (10) + Extreme scale (10)
532: 
533: **Suggested phase counts:**
534: - Score 25-34: 2 phases
535: - Score 35-44: 3 phases
536: - Score 45+: 4 phases
537: 
538: ### Phase Folder Pattern
539: 
540: ```
541: specs/###-parent/
542: ├── spec.md           # Phase Documentation Map
543: ├── 001-phase-one/    # Independent child spec folder
544: ├── 002-phase-two/
545: └── 003-phase-three/
546: ```
547: 
548: ### Phase vs Version Sub-Folders
549: 
550: - **Phases:** Parallel decomposition of different work streams
551: - **Versions:** Sequential iterations of the same work
552: 
553: **Full documentation:** See [phase-definitions.md](../structure/phase-definitions.md)

557: ## 17. AGENT CRITICAL RULES (PROGRESSIVE ENHANCEMENT)
558: 
559: ### Absolutely Required
560: 
561: - **NEVER create documentation from scratch** - Always copy from templates
562: - **ALWAYS copy from `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/`** directory
563: - **ALWAYS copy ALL REQUIRED templates for chosen level**:
564:   - Level 1: spec.md + plan.md + tasks.md + implementation-summary.md
565:   - Level 2: Level 1 + acceptance-criteria.md
566:   - Level 3: Level 2 file set (decision-record.md on request)
567: - **ALWAYS fill ALL placeholders** - No `<PLACEHOLDER>` marker in final docs
568: - **ALWAYS respond to workflow prompts** - Ask user for A/B/C/D choice
569: - **ALWAYS get user approval** - Explicit "yes" before file changes
570: - **Use distributed governance for spec docs** — Any agent writing packet markdown must use the level templates, run `validate.sh --strict`, and route continuity refreshes through `/speckit:save`. Preserve `@deep-research` ownership of `research/research.md` and `@debug` ownership of `debug-delegation.md`.
571: 
572: ### Enforcement
573: 
574: - **Verify required templates exist** before claiming completion
575: - **LOC is one scored input** - run `recommend-level.sh` and go higher when your judgment disagrees
576: - **Enforcement is `validate.sh --strict` plus `check-completion.sh`** - run both before claiming done
577: 
578: ### Applies to ALL
579: 
580: - Code files (*.js, *.ts, *.py, *.css, *.html)
581: - Documentation files (*.md, README, docs/)
582: - Configuration files (*.json, *.yaml, *.toml)
583: - Knowledge base files (project-specific)
584: - Template files (.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/*.md)
585: - Build files (package.json, requirements.txt)
586: 
587: **No exceptions** (unless user explicitly selects Option D)

591: ## 18. CHECKLIST VERIFICATION PROTOCOL (LEVEL 2+)
592: 
593: ### When to Use
594: 
595: Checklist verification is **MANDATORY** for all Level 2+ documentation:
596: - Level 2: Features requiring QA validation (100-499 LOC guidance)
597: - Level 3: Complex/architectural work (>=500 LOC guidance)
598: - Level 3+: Complex governance/multi-agent work (high complexity/risk)
599: 
600: The verification region of `tasks.md` is an **ACTIVE VERIFICATION TOOL**, not passive documentation.
601: 
602: ### Verification Process
603: 
604: ```
605: CHECKLIST AS VERIFICATION TOOL (Level 2+):
606: 1. LOAD the tasks.md verification region at completion phase
607: 2. VERIFY each item systematically (P0 first, then P1, then P2)
608: 3. MARK items [x] with evidence (links, test results, etc.)
609: 4. BLOCK completion until all P0/P1 items verified
610: 5. DOCUMENT any deferred P2 items with reason
611: ```
612: 
613: ### Priority Levels
614: 
615: | Priority | Meaning | Completion Gate |
616: |----------|---------|-----------------|
617: | **P0** | Blocker | MUST pass - work is incomplete without this |
618: | **P1** | Required | MUST pass - required for production readiness |
619: | **P2** | Optional | Can defer with documented reason |
620: 
621: ### How to Verify Items
622: 
623: For each checklist item:
624: 
625: 1. **Perform the check** (run test, inspect code, verify behavior)
626: 2. **Mark with [x]** when verified
627: 3. **Add evidence** (link, test output, screenshot reference)
628: 4. **Add timestamp** for audit trail
629: 
630: ### Example: Properly Verified Checklist
631: 
632: ```markdown
633: ## Verification Checklist
634: 
635: ### P0 - Blockers (MUST pass)
636: - [x] Core functionality works as specified
637:   - Evidence: Manual test passed - modal opens/closes correctly
638:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:30
639: - [x] No console errors in browser
640:   - Evidence: DevTools console clean on Chrome/Firefox/Safari
641:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:32
642: 
643: ### P1 - Required (MUST pass for production)
644: - [x] Responsive design verified (mobile/tablet/desktop)
645:   - Evidence: Tested at 375px, 768px, 1440px breakpoints
646:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:35
647: - [x] Accessibility: keyboard navigation works
648:   - Evidence: Tab/Enter/Escape all functional
649:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:38
650: 
651: ### P2 - Optional (can defer)
652: - [ ] Performance optimization for large datasets
653:   - Deferred: Not needed for MVP, tracked in issue #123
654: - [x] Animation smoothness verified
655:   - Evidence: 60fps confirmed in Performance tab
656:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:40
657: ```
658: 
659: ### AI Agent Rules
660: 
661: - **NEVER claim completion without running checklist verification**
662: - **ALWAYS load the tasks.md verification region before stating work is done**
663: - **ALWAYS mark items with evidence, not only [x]**
664: - **ALWAYS complete all P0/P1 before claiming done**
665: - **ALWAYS document why P2 items are deferred (if applicable)**
666: 
667: ---

669: ## 19. CORE PRINCIPLE
670: 
671: **Every file change deserves documentation.**
672: 
673: Future you will thank present you for creating that spec folder.

676: - Document more rather than less

102: ## 4. ESSENTIAL COMMANDS

104: ### Start Here: Command Map

106: If the runtime does not surface command menus clearly, use this compact command map first.

108: **SpecKit workflow commands**
109: - `/speckit:resume` - continue or recover existing spec-folder work
110: - `/speckit:plan` - define or refine a scoped spec and plan
111: - `/speckit:implement` - execute an existing spec and plan packet

227: ## 8. UPDATE, PHASE, OR CREATE DECISION
228: 
229: ### CONTINUE or UPDATE Existing Work When:
230: 
231: ✅ Iterative development of the same feature
232: ✅ Bug fixes to the existing implementation
233: ✅ Scope escalation within the same outcome
234: ✅ Enhancement of existing functionality
235: ✅ Resuming paused work
236: ✅ The request fits the active packet's purpose, scope, requirements, or Phase Documentation Map
237: 
238: ### PREFER A PHASED PACKET When:
239: 
240: ✅ The work is related to one coordinated outcome
241: ✅ Phase complexity score >= 25 AND documentation level >= 3
242: ✅ The work contains distinct workstreams that would otherwise become separate top-level single-spec folders
243: ✅ The work is a different change to the same artifact as an existing packet in the same track (a series parent, `phase-definitions.md` §2)
244: 
245: The phased-packet preference does not override qualification. If only one or neither threshold is met and no series parent qualifies, continue or update a standard non-phased packet.
246: 
247: ### CREATE New Top-Level Work When:
248: 
249: ❌ Distinct feature with a separate outcome
250: ❌ Different requirement or separate user story outside the current scope
251: ❌ Alternative strategy that must remain independently governed
252: ❌ Complete redesign that supersedes rather than extends the current packet
253: ❌ Unrelated work with no requirement, implementation, or dependency continuity
254: 
255: New/unrelated work is allowed to use Option B, but the new packet must still be evaluated independently. If it meets both phase thresholds, create a new phased packet; otherwise create a standard packet.
256: 
257: **Phased Packets:** If the target already has child phase folders, use the active child when the work fits that child's scope. For a distinct but related workstream, prefer Option C and add the next sequential child phase instead of creating a new top-level sibling packet. Use the coordination root only for phase-map updates, root-scope decisions, and tree-truth verification. Use Option B only when the work is outside the phase parent's documented purpose and scope.
258: 
259: **Small-task definition:** "Small" means exempt work or work that remains Level 1 after LOC guidance and all secondary risk/complexity factors are applied. A Level 2 or Level 3 task that does not phase-qualify is not automatically "small"; it remains standard because the phase thresholds were not both met.

263: ## 9. CONFIRMATION OPTIONS
264: 
265: When Gate 3 applies, always present all four stable labels and ask the user to choose:
266: 
267: **Option A:** Continue in the detected/current spec or current phase child when its scope fits.
268: **Option B:** Create a new top-level packet for new/unrelated work; independently evaluate whether that new packet qualifies for phases.
269: **Option C:** Use another existing packet — a related spec when it is a better scope match, a specific child under an existing phase parent, a related standard packet decomposed into phases when it meets both phase thresholds, or a series parent when the work is a different change to the same artifact as an existing packet in the same track (phase-definitions.md §2).
270: **Option D:** Skip spec documentation after the required warning or under an existing exemption.
271: 
272: **Recommendation priority:** `C` for a distinct related workstream in an existing or qualifying phased packet, including a series parent; otherwise `A` when the current packet fits; otherwise `C` for another related packet; `B` only for new/unrelated work; `D` is never the default.
273: 
274: **AI Agent Rule:** Recommend the best-fit option using this priority, but NEVER select it autonomously. The user must choose A/B/C/D.

465: ## 15. CONTEXT SAVE & HANDOVER
466: 
467: ### Context Save
468: 
469: **Manual triggers (OpenCode):**
470: - Command: `/speckit:save`
471: - Keywords: "save context", "save conversation", "save this"
472: 
473: **Note:** OpenCode does not support automatic interval-based saves (hooks are event-triggered via plugins, not time-interval).
474: 
475: **MANDATORY:** Use generate-context.js for memory save:
476: ```
477: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js /tmp/save-context-data-<session-id>.json specs/###-folder/
478: ```
479: 
480: Use `generate-context.js` for routine metadata and index saves. Quick direct edits are allowed only for `_memory.continuity` YAML frontmatter blocks in `implementation-summary.md`.
481: 
482: > **Recovery Integration:** Packet recovery is canonical-first. Start from `handover.md`, then `_memory.continuity` in `implementation-summary.md`, then the rest of the packet docs before widening with a ripgrep sweep over the specs tree.
483: 
484: **Phased Resume**: When the target folder has child phases, first resolve
485: whether you need the coordination root or an active child.
486: Load/save memory in the child packet by default.
487: Only load root memory when updating coordination snapshots.
488: 
489: **Phase-Parent Resume Ladder**: When the resume target is a phase parent (folder has `[0-9]{3}-name/` children with `spec.md` or `description.json`), `/speckit:resume` honors the pointer first:
490: 
491: 1. Read the pointer, from the telemetry store first and then from `derived.last_active_child_id` in the parent's `graph-metadata.json`. When it names an existing child packet inside the parent, recurse into that child at any age, report the child and its `derived.last_active_at`, and apply the child's normal handover → `_memory.continuity` → spec docs ladder. Confirm mode asks first when the pointer is older than 24 hours.
492: 2. If the pointer is null, missing, malformed, points outside the parent, or names a child that no longer exists, fall back to listing children with statuses (sourced from each child's `graph-metadata.json` `derived.status`) and let the user pick.
493: 3. `--no-redirect` flag bypasses the pointer step entirely and shows the parent's spec.md plus child list.
494: 
495: The pointer is maintained automatically by the generator: a save into a child points every phase-parent ancestor one level down toward it. A save aimed at a phase parent moves the pointers only when a `--full-auto` save routes its continuity into a leaf, and otherwise moves none. A track root keeps its pointer in the telemetry store only. Atomic write via temp+rename. No `_memory.continuity` block exists at a phase parent (per the lean trio policy — parents have no `implementation-summary.md`).
496: 
497: **Save location:**
498: - Primary: the active packet's canonical continuity surfaces
499: - Core continuity block: `_memory.continuity` in `implementation-summary.md`
500: - No workspace-root fallback; direct CLI targets stay inside the selected root spec or phase packet
501: 
502: ### Session Continuity Save
503: 
504: **Command:** `/speckit:save`
505: 
506: **Purpose:** Refresh packet continuity before a pause or handoff while keeping `handover.md`, `_memory.continuity`, and the packet docs aligned for the next `/speckit:resume` pass.
507: 
508: **Use when:**
509: - Ending a long session
510: - Context compaction detected
511: - Handing off to another session
512: - Before complex multi-step operations

516: ## 16. PHASE WORKFLOW SHORTCUTS
517: 
518: ### Phase Commands
519: 
520: | Command | Description |
521: |---------|-------------|
522: | `/speckit:plan :with-phases` | Trigger phase decomposition as pre-workflow in plan or complete |
523: | `create.sh --phase --phases N --phase-names a,b,c <description>` | Create a phase parent and named child phase folders |
524: | `create.sh --phase --parent <parent> --phases N --phase-names a,b <description>` | Add named child phases to an existing parent spec |
525: | `validate.sh <parent> --recursive` | Validate parent and all child phase folders |
526: 
527: ### Phase Quick Reference
528: 
529: **Detection:** Complexity score >= 25 AND level >= 3, or a series parent for a different change to the same artifact
530: 
531: **Scoring dimensions:** Architectural (10) + Files>15 (10) + LOC>800 (10) + Risk>=2 (10) + Extreme scale (10)
532: 
533: **Suggested phase counts:**
534: - Score 25-34: 2 phases
535: - Score 35-44: 3 phases
536: - Score 45+: 4 phases
537: 
538: ### Phase Folder Pattern
539: 
540: ```
541: specs/###-parent/
542: ├── spec.md           # Phase Documentation Map
543: ├── 001-phase-one/    # Independent child spec folder
544: ├── 002-phase-two/
545: └── 003-phase-three/
546: ```
547: 
548: ### Phase vs Version Sub-Folders
549: 
550: - **Phases:** Parallel decomposition of different work streams
551: - **Versions:** Sequential iterations of the same work
552: 
553: **Full documentation:** See [phase-definitions.md](../structure/phase-definitions.md)

591: ## 18. CHECKLIST VERIFICATION PROTOCOL (LEVEL 2+)
592: 
593: ### When to Use
594: 
595: Checklist verification is **MANDATORY** for all Level 2+ documentation:
596: - Level 2: Features requiring QA validation (100-499 LOC guidance)
597: - Level 3: Complex/architectural work (>=500 LOC guidance)
598: - Level 3+: Complex governance/multi-agent work (high complexity/risk)
599: 
600: The verification region of `tasks.md` is an **ACTIVE VERIFICATION TOOL**, not passive documentation.
601: 
602: ### Verification Process
603: 
604: ```
605: CHECKLIST AS VERIFICATION TOOL (Level 2+):
606: 1. LOAD the tasks.md verification region at completion phase
607: 2. VERIFY each item systematically (P0 first, then P1, then P2)
608: 3. MARK items [x] with evidence (links, test results, etc.)
609: 4. BLOCK completion until all P0/P1 items verified
610: 5. DOCUMENT any deferred P2 items with reason
611: ```
612: 
613: ### Priority Levels
614: 
615: | Priority | Meaning | Completion Gate |
616: |----------|---------|-----------------|
617: | **P0** | Blocker | MUST pass - work is incomplete without this |
618: | **P1** | Required | MUST pass - required for production readiness |
619: | **P2** | Optional | Can defer with documented reason |
620: 
621: ### How to Verify Items
622: 
623: For each checklist item:
624: 
625: 1. **Perform the check** (run test, inspect code, verify behavior)
626: 2. **Mark with [x]** when verified
627: 3. **Add evidence** (link, test output, screenshot reference)
628: 4. **Add timestamp** for audit trail
629: 
630: ### Example: Properly Verified Checklist
631: 
632: ```markdown
633: ## Verification Checklist
634: 
635: ### P0 - Blockers (MUST pass)
636: - [x] Core functionality works as specified
637:   - Evidence: Manual test passed - modal opens/closes correctly
638:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:30
639: - [x] No console errors in browser
640:   - Evidence: DevTools console clean on Chrome/Firefox/Safari
641:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:32
642: 
643: ### P1 - Required (MUST pass for production)
644: - [x] Responsive design verified (mobile/tablet/desktop)
645:   - Evidence: Tested at 375px, 768px, 1440px breakpoints
646:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:35
647: - [x] Accessibility: keyboard navigation works
648:   - Evidence: Tab/Enter/Escape all functional
649:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:38
650: 
651: ### P2 - Optional (can defer)
652: - [ ] Performance optimization for large datasets
653:   - Deferred: Not needed for MVP, tracked in issue #123
654: - [x] Animation smoothness verified
655:   - Evidence: 60fps confirmed in Performance tab
656:   - Verified: 2025-12-01 14:40
657: ```
658: 
659: ### AI Agent Rules
660: 
661: - **NEVER claim completion without running checklist verification**
662: - **ALWAYS load the tasks.md verification region before stating work is done**
663: - **ALWAYS mark items with evidence, not only [x]**
664: - **ALWAYS complete all P0/P1 before claiming done**
665: - **ALWAYS document why P2 items are deferred (if applicable)**

19:

21: 
22: ### Purpose
23:

25:

27: 
28: Load this reference before a repo-wide rename that touches more than one live surface or when auditing whether historical surfaces should be preserved.
29: 
30: ### Core Principle
31:

35: 
36: ## 2. SURFACE TAXONOMY
37: 
38: Every rename touches some subset of these categories. Map each before starting.
39: 
40: | Category | Examples | How to handle |
41: |---|---|---|
42: | **The thing being renamed** | `.skilled/skills/<old>/` dir or `.skilled/agents/<old>.md` | `git mv` (preserves history) |
43: | **Live cross-references** | Sibling skill `graph-metadata.json` `enhances`/`related_to`, command files, manual playbooks | Literal substitution |
44: | **Live runtime mirrors** | `.claude/agents/`, `.skilled/agents/` + corresponding READMEs | `git mv` + literal substitution |
45: | **Live root behavioral docs** | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (often symlinked), `README.md` | Literal substitution |
46: | **Live auto-memory** | `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/MEMORY.md` index + current-state memory files | Literal substitution; preserve filename slugs to avoid breaking inbound `[[wikilinks]]` |
47: | **Live compiled indexes** | `skill-graph.json`, SQLite caches | REGENERATE (never hand-edit) |
48: | **Historical narrative** | Memory feedback entries describing past incidents under the old name | Tag inline: `(renamed <new> YYYY-MM-DD)` — keep dates intact |
49: | **Historical spec docs** | Originating packet's `spec.md`/`plan.md`/`tasks.md`/`acceptance-criteria.md`/`implementation-summary.md` | PRESERVE — do not edit |
50: | **Historical research/review iterations** | Deep-research / deep-review `iterations/*.md`, `deltas/*.jsonl` | PRESERVE — do not edit |
51: | **Historical version notes** | Renamed skill's prior `changelog/v*.md` | PRESERVE — add a NEW `vN+1.0.0.md` as forward-link |
52: | **Frozen bench fixtures** | `benchmarks/.../per-probe.jsonl` recording prior-name state | PRESERVE |
53: 
54: **Rule of thumb**: If the surface describes work as it happened in the past, preserve. If the surface describes what is true NOW, update.

63: 3. Read the cli-X SKILL.md file before composing any cli-X dispatch (per AGENTS.md CLI dispatch rule).
64: 
65: ### Phase B — Optional CLI verification
66: Dispatch 2-4 parallel read-only CLI jobs (e.g. cli-opencode or cli-opencode) to verify the rename plan against each surface group. Read the chosen executor's SKILL.md before composing the dispatch (per AGENTS.md CLI dispatch rule). Apply bundle gate per the `feedback_bundle_gate_smoke_run` memory note. Aggregate verified bundles.
67: 
68: ### Phase C — Execute renames (parallel-eligible across disjoint surface groups)
69: 1. `git mv` dir/file renames (preserves rename history; `git log --follow` traces back).
70: 2. Bulk literal substitution via `sed -i ''` (macOS) on the in-scope file list. Use `find -exec` for atomicity across many files.
71: 3. Special-case the historical-narrative file with surgical edits (insert `(renamed <new> YYYY-MM-DD)` tag rather than rewriting).
72: 4. Memory files: filename slugs are sticky (preserve `[[wikilinks]]`); only edit body content.
73: 
74: ### Phase D — Reindex
75: 1. Regenerate compiled `.skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill-graph.json` via `python3 skill_graph_compiler.py --export-json --pretty` (per the `feedback_skill_graph_compiler_rebuild` memory note).
76: 2. If the compiler hits a pre-existing blocker (wrong category, asymmetric sibling, etc.), fix it incidentally — document as out-of-scope-but-on-critical-path.
77: 3. Run `advisor_recommend` MCP smoke on a canonical prompt for the renamed thing; expect new name in top-3 confidence ≥ 0.7.
78: 
79: ### Phase E — Validate
80: 1. Post-edit `rg "<old-name>"` on the live-surface allow-list → expect 0 hits.
81: 2. Post-edit `rg "<old-name>"` on the historical-surface allow-list → expect SAME count as baseline-before (provenance preserved).
82: 3. `bash validate.sh --strict <spec-folder>` → exit 0.
83: 4. Reconcile parent metadata via `generate-context.js` (refreshes `children_ids` + `derived.last_active_child_id`).

85:

87: 
88: ## 4. CASE-SENSITIVITY GOTCHA
89: 
90: Per the `feedback_rename_grep_case_insensitive` memory note: the final-gate grep MUST use `rg -il` (case-insensitive). UPPERCASE / Title-Case / underscore variants are easy to miss. Always also check for the underscore variant of any hyphenated identifier (e.g., `sk_small_model` next to `sk-small-model`) — Python pseudocode in `ROUTER.md` examples often uses underscores.
91: 
92: ---
93:

95: 
96: Per the `feedback_stay_on_main_no_feature_branches` memory note — stay on `main`. `create.sh` auto-branches; switch back to `main` and delete the auto-created branch (carry uncommitted changes; cherry-pick any orphan continuity commits first).
97: 
98: Rename refactors are reversible via `git revert` since `git mv` history is preserved. No need to feature-branch.
99: 
100: ---
101:

103: 
104: When the rename arc is a phase-parent with multiple children:
105: - Each phase child's `spec.md` §3 In Scope + Out of Scope is the conflict-prevention contract.
106: - The rename-plan.json from preflight enforces disjoint file scopes across phase children.
107: - Phases that touch disjoint file sets can be executed in parallel by separate operators.

114: |---|---|---|
115: | Hand-editing compiled `skill-graph.json` | Compiled artifact gets overwritten next compile | Regenerate via `skill_graph_compiler.py` |
116: | Renaming auto-memory file slugs | Breaks inbound `[[wikilinks]]` in MEMORY.md and other memory files | Preserve slug; edit body content only |
117: | Rewriting historical narrative to use new name | Falsifies past-tense provenance | Insert `(renamed <new> YYYY-MM-DD)` tag |
118: | Editing the renamed skill's own `changelog/v1+v2*.md` | Historical version state | Add NEW `vN+1.0.0.md` as forward-link |
119: | Creating a feature branch | Out of policy (the `feedback_stay_on_main_no_feature_branches` memory note) | Stay on `main`; `git revert` is the rollback path |
120: | Forgetting case variants | Misses `sk_small_model` (underscore), `Sk-Small-Model` (title), `SK-SMALL-MODEL` (banner) | Use `rg -il` and dedicated 2nd sed pass for underscore identifiers |
121: 
122: ---

125:

127: - spec.md §3 In Scope / Out of Scope is the model classifier

129: - implementation-summary.md §What Was Built lists the actual surface counts (22 live files, 5 dir/file renames, 1 new changelog)
130: - review-report.md (deep-review 9-iter PASS+advisories) verifies the pattern's correctness

132: ---

137: - [ ] Per-file live/historical classification written to `scratch/resource-map.md`
138: - [ ] Disjoint phase scopes in `scratch/rename-plan.json` (jq intersection check = empty)
139: - [ ] cli-X SKILL.md read before composing any cli-X dispatch
140: - [ ] All `git mv` renames execute cleanly
141: - [ ] `sed -i ''` bulk pass (hyphenated form)
142: - [ ] Second sed pass for underscore variants (where applicable)
143: - [ ] Auto-memory filename slugs preserved; only body content edited
144: - [ ] Historical-narrative files tagged inline, not rewritten
145: - [ ] New `vN+1.0.0.md` changelog created on the renamed skill
146: - [ ] Compiled `skill-graph.json` regenerated via `skill_graph_compiler.py`
147: - [ ] `advisor_recommend` smoke confirms new name surfaces ≥ 0.7
148: - [ ] Live-surface rg returns 0 hits
149: - [ ] Historical-surface rg returns SAME count as baseline-before
150: - [ ] `validate.sh --strict <spec-folder>` exit 0

14: # Spec Authoring Card
15: 
16: This card is the short path. Follow the steps in order. Each step has one action, one acceptance line and one command. When the command prints what the acceptance line says, go to the next step.
17: 
18: `references/templates/template-guide.md` is the long guide. Read it only when a section's fill note leaves you unsure what to write.
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW AND BOUNDS
21: 
22: You write one packet, in one folder. The folder is the one `create.sh` prints.
23: 
24: Allowed writes: the packet folder and its `scratch/` folder.
25: Forbidden: `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js`, `/speckit:save`. Do not edit `.skilled/`, another packet or a source file. Do not run `create.sh` twice.
26: 
27: Acceptance: you can name the packet folder and the one command you will run to check it.
28: Verify: `pwd` prints the repository root, and `ls <packet folder>` lists `spec.md`.
29: 
30: ---
31: 
32: ## 2. PICK THE LEVEL
33: 
34: Run the level helper first.
35: 
36: ```bash
37: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh --loc <lines> --files <count>
38: ```
39: 
40: Use the level it prints. If it prints Level 0, use `--level 1`. Do not raise the level yourself. The level decides which files the packet needs.
41: 
42: | Level | Files the packet needs |
43: |-------|------------------------|
44: | 1 | `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and `implementation-summary.md` once implementation starts |
45: | 2 | the Level 1 files plus `acceptance-criteria.md` |
46: | 3 | the Level 2 files plus the architecture sections and a decision record when one is written |
47: 
48: Acceptance: the level in the scaffold header matches the level the helper printed.

50:

54: 
55: Create the packet with one command. Keep `--skip-branch` so no git state changes.
56: 
57: ```bash
58: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh --skip-branch --with-goal --level <level> --track <track> --short-name <two-to-four-words> "<one sentence>"

14: # Spec Folder Authoring Checklist
15: 
16: Checklist for writing spec folders that satisfy the Level contract, continuity frontmatter, metadata files, and strict validation.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Purpose
21: 
22: This checklist keeps spec folder writes compatible with the system-spec-kit validator and memory resume ladder. It is the companion checklist to the spec folder write recipe and focuses on required files, anchors, metadata, and strict validation.
23: 
24: ### Usage
25: 
26: - Use this when authoring a new spec folder under `specs/` or `.opencode/specs/`.
27: - Use this when modifying a spec folder's canonical docs, frontmatter, `_memory.continuity`, or metadata files.
28: - Use this when creating a phase child under a phase parent.
29: - Use this when a workflow writes `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `implementation-summary.md`, `description.json`, or `graph-metadata.json`.
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 2. PRE-CHECKS
34: 
35: - [ ] Read the Level 1 contract files in `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/examples/level-1/`.
36: - [ ] Read one rendered example under `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/examples/` or a fresh `create.sh` scaffold. Do not copy from a `.tmpl` source: it carries unfilled tokens.
37: - [ ] Verify the required Level 1 docs: `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and `implementation-summary.md`.
38: - [ ] Confirm required anchor counts for the selected level before writing.
39: - [ ] Confirm `_memory.continuity.packet_pointer` is slash-separated and relative to the specs track.
40: - [ ] Confirm `description.json` and `graph-metadata.json` will be refreshed after authoring.
41: - [ ] Before creating a new top-level packet, check whether the current work is inside a phase parent.
42: - [ ] If it is, compare the request with the parent `spec.md` purpose, scope, requirements, and Phase Documentation Map.
43: - [ ] Continue in the current child when its scope fits; otherwise prefer a new child phase for a distinct related workstream. Create a separate top-level packet only for new/unrelated work.
44: - [ ] Do not convert a standard packet into a phase parent unless phase complexity score >= 25 AND documentation level >= 3, or the new work is a different change to the same artifact in the same track, which makes a series parent (`../structure/phase-definitions.md` §2).
45: 
46: ---
47: 
48: ## 3. STEPS
49: 
50: 1. Decide the spec root, packet number, short name, phase child name, and documentation level.
51: 2. Scaffold from system-spec-kit templates or `create.sh` instead of freehanding the contract.
52: 3. Author `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and `implementation-summary.md` with canonical anchors.
53: 4. Add `_memory.continuity` frontmatter with compact `recent_action`, ISO-8601 UTC `last_updated_at`, and a full relative `packet_pointer`.
54: 5. Refresh `description.json` and `graph-metadata.json` with the system-spec-kit metadata scripts.
55: 6. Run strict validation and fix every warning as a failure.
56: 7. Record verification evidence in the implementation summary or handoff output.
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 4. POST-CHECKS
61: 
62: - [ ] Run `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <path> --strict`.
63: - [ ] grep verification: `rg -n "ANCHOR:metadata|ANCHOR:summary|ANCHOR:notation|_memory:|packet_pointer" <path>`.
64: - [ ] grep verification: `rg -n "\"title\"|\"contextType\"|\"derived\"" <path>/description.json <path>/graph-metadata.json`.
65: - [ ] Cross-runtime mirror parity check if the spec folder changes command or agent mirrors.
66: - [ ] Confirm the companion recipe was followed: `spec-folder-write-recipe.md`.
67: 
68: ---
69: 
70: ## 5. RELATED RESOURCES
71: 
72: - sk-doc templates and system-spec-kit/templates/ (source-of-truth for document contract rules)
73: - Prior example: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/examples/level-1/`
74: - Verification recipes: `spec-folder-write-recipe.md`

31: 
32: ### Step 1: Scaffold via create.sh
33: 
34: Run the system-spec-kit scaffold from the repository root:
35: 
36: ```bash
37: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh \
38:   --skip-branch \
39:   --short-name "opencode-authoring-recipe" \
40:   --number 078 \
41:   --level 1
42: ```
43: 
44: Verification gate: confirm the scaffolded folder exists and contains the expected Level contract files.
45: 
46: ### Step 2: Move to track
47: 
48: Move the scaffolded folder from the default location into the selected track, for example:
49: 
50: ```bash
51: mv specs/078-opencode-authoring-recipe \
52:   specs/system-speckit/078-opencode-authoring-recipe
53: ```
54: 
55: The `system-speckit` track in the destination above is an example, so substitute the track you chose in the pre-conditions.
56:

58:

60: 
61: - `spec.md` (7 anchors: metadata, problem, scope, requirements, success-criteria, risks, questions)
62: - `plan.md` (7 anchors: summary, quality-gates, architecture, phases, testing, dependencies, rollback)
63: - `tasks.md` (6 anchors: notation, phase-1, phase-2, phase-3, completion, cross-refs; phase headers MUST be canonical "Phase 1: Setup" / "Phase 2: Implementation" / "Phase 3: Verification")
64: - `implementation-summary.md` (6 anchors: metadata, what-built, how-delivered, decisions, verification, limitations)
65:

67: 
68: ### Step 4: Frontmatter `_memory.continuity` block
69: 
70: - `packet_pointer`: slash-separated relative path (NOT just folder name)
71: - `recent_action`: keep compact (NOT verbose multi-clause)
72: - `last_updated_at`: ISO-8601 UTC
73:

75: 
76: ### Step 5: Refresh metadata
77: 
78: ```bash
79: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/spec-folder/generate-description.js \
80:   <folder> \
81:   <repo-root> \
82:   --description "Short description for memory search" \
83:   --level N
84: 
85: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/graph/backfill-graph-metadata.js \
86:   <folder>
87: ```
88: 
89: Verification gate: confirm `description.json` and `graph-metadata.json` exist and describe the same folder.
90: 
91: ### Step 6: validate.sh --strict gate
92: 
93: ```bash
94: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <folder> --strict
95: ```
96: 
97: Must print `RESULT: PASSED` with 0 errors. A warning does not fail `--strict`, so read each one and fix the ones that are real.
98: 
99: Common pitfalls: `SPECDOC_SUFFICIENCY_004` (research.md needs anchor + citation pattern), `TEMPLATE_HEADERS` (canonical phase header names required), `ANCHORS_VALID` (full 7/7/6/6 anchor count per doc-type).
100: 
101: ### Step 7: Commit + push
102: 
103: - Workspace: use the one the operator chose, a worktree or the current branch. Never pick it yourself and never create a branch with git primitives (see "Workspace Choice Enforcement" in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md`). `main` is on the remote allowlist, so pushing it needs no extra approval, and a branch off the allowlist needs the operator's go-ahead for that push (see "Remote Push Permission Enforcement" in the same file).
104: - Subject: `type(subsystem): summary`. Take the type from the first match in the priority list in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md` (a doc-only packet is `docs`) and name the owning subsystem as the scope, such as `spec-kit`. Never use the packet number or path as the scope.
105: - Body: at least one prose line that says why. Trailers do not count as a body.
106: - Trailers: `Spec: <track>/<packet>`, the packet's path below `specs/` without the `specs/` segment. `prepare-commit-msg` stamps `Commit-Id:`, so never type it.
107: - No attribution trailers. The `commit-msg` hook refuses `Co-Authored-By:` and `Claude-Session:`.
108: 
109: The full contract is `.skilled/skills/sk-git/assets/commit-message-template.md`.
110: 
111: Verification gate: stage the packet files by explicit path, then confirm `git diff --cached --name-only` lists only the intended packet files before commit. In a shared tree `git status --short` also lists other sessions' changes, so it cannot be the test (see "Step 7: Scoped-Staging Discipline" in `.skilled/skills/sk-git/references/commit-workflows.md`).

114: 
115: ## 4. POST-CHECKS
116: 
117: - [ ] validate.sh --strict exit 0

119: - [ ] The commit reached origin on the branch you worked on (the Workspace bullet in Step 7 says which pushes need approval)
120: - [ ] /speckit:save via generate-context.js (optional but recommended)
121:

125:

127: |---|---|
128: | TEMPLATE_HEADERS error | tasks.md must use canonical "Phase 1: Setup" / "Phase 2: Implementation" / "Phase 3: Verification" headers |
129: | ANCHORS_VALID error | plan.md needs all 7 anchors (summary/quality-gates/architecture/phases/testing/dependencies/rollback) |
130: | SPECDOC_SUFFICIENCY_004 | research.md needs at least one ANCHOR block containing a citation pattern (file path in backticks, markdown link, or "iteration-N" reference) |
131: | FRONTMATTER_VALID error on packet_pointer | Use the full slash-separated relative path for the active work packet, not only its leaf folder name |
132:

139: - system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/spec-folder/generate-description.js (metadata refresh)
140: - system-spec-kit/templates/{spec,plan,tasks,implementation-summary}.md.tmpl (canonical templates)

# Skill ARCHITECTURE.md Template

Use this template for the `ARCHITECTURE.md` at a skill package root, next to `SKILL.md` and `README.md`. It explains how the package's code works as a system. The README orients a user, `SKILL.md` routes an agent, and `ARCHITECTURE.md` tells a maintainer where behavior lives and which way dependencies run.

---

## 1. WHEN TO USE

Write an `ARCHITECTURE.md` when a skill package ships runtime code: a daemon, a CLI, a library, hooks or scripts with more than one layer. A documentation-only skill does not need one.

A code-folder README (`readme-code-template.md`) covers one folder. `ARCHITECTURE.md` covers the whole package: how its zones relate, the paths data takes through them, and what enforces the contract. When a folder README starts explaining other folders, that explanation belongs here.

---

## 2. CONTENT MODEL

The eight sections are fixed and numbered in this order, so a reader moving between skills finds the same thing in the same place. A section with nothing to say states that in one line rather than disappearing.

| Section | Holds | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1. OVERVIEW | What the package does, its front door, its authored zones, and an architecture diagram | One or two paragraphs plus the diagram |
| 2. PACKAGE TOPOLOGY | A directory tree of the package with one-line roles, and the allowed dependency direction | Show only folders that matter; list import edges as `a/ ──▶ b/` |
| 3. CANONICAL FLOWS | The main read path and write path, each named after its entry command, plus the module that owns each | Keep to the paths that define the package |
| 4. RUNTIME SUBSYSTEMS | One bolded paragraph per subsystem: what it does and where it lives | Link reference docs for depth instead of repeating them |
| 5. HOOK AND PLUGIN INTEGRATION | How runtimes, hooks, plugins or other skills call in, and what happens on timeout or failure | Write "None" when the package has no integration surface |
| 6. ENFORCEMENT AND VERIFICATION | The checks that hold the contract: validators, test suites, benchmarks, playbooks | Name the command or folder for each |
| 7. DECISION RECORDS | A table of the architecture decisions still in force, with status | Local numbering only; no spec or packet ids |
| 8. RELATED | Links to README, SKILL.md, install guide, feature catalog, playbook and references | Relative links from the package root |

---

## 3. WRITING RULES

- Describe current reality. Planned behavior goes in a spec, not here.
- Name files and folders by their real paths so a reader can open them.
- Draw the diagram with Unicode box characters inside a `text` fence, following the diagrams in `readme-code-template.md` §3.
- Keep it evergreen: no spec paths, packet numbers, phase names or task ids. The decision table numbers its own rows.
- Update §2 whenever a folder is added, merged or renamed, because the topology is what goes stale first.

---

     2	
     3	> **Recovery Integration:** Packet recovery is canonical-first. Start from `handover.md`, then `_memory.continuity` in `implementation-summary.md`, then the rest of the packet docs before widening with a ripgrep sweep over the specs tree.
     4	
     5	**Phased Resume**: When the target folder has child phases, first resolve
     6	whether you need the coordination root or an active child.
     7	Load/save memory in the child packet by default.
     8	Only load root memory when updating coordination snapshots.
     9	
    10	**Phase-Parent Resume Ladder**: When the resume target is a phase parent (folder has `[0-9]{3}-name/` children with `spec.md` or `description.json`), `/speckit:resume` honors the pointer first:
    11	
    12	1. Read the pointer, from the telemetry store first and then from `derived.last_active_child_id` in the parent's `graph-metadata.json`. When it names an existing child packet inside the parent, recurse into that child at any age, report the child and its `derived.last_active_at`, and apply the child's normal handover → `_memory.continuity` → spec docs ladder. Confirm mode asks first when the pointer is older than 24 hours.
    13	2. If the pointer is null, missing, malformed, points outside the parent, or names a child that no longer exists, fall back to listing children with statuses (sourced from each child's `graph-metadata.json` `derived.status`) and let the user pick.
    14	3. `--no-redirect` flag bypasses the pointer step entirely and shows the parent's spec.md plus child list.
    15	
    16	The pointer is maintained automatically by the generator: a save into a child points every phase-parent ancestor one level down toward it. A save aimed at a phase parent moves the pointers only when a `--full-auto` save routes its continuity into a leaf, and otherwise moves none. A track root keeps its pointer in the telemetry store only. Atomic write via temp+rename. No `_memory.continuity` block exists at a phase parent (per the lean trio policy — parents have no `implementation-summary.md`).
    17	
    18	**Save location:**
    19	- Primary: the active packet's canonical continuity surfaces
    20	- Core continuity block: `_memory.continuity` in `implementation-summary.md`
    21	- No workspace-root fallback; direct CLI targets stay inside the selected root spec or phase packet

# Validation Rules Reference - Complete Rule Reference

Complete reference for all validation rules used by the SpecKit validation system.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### What Is This Reference?

This document provides comprehensive documentation for every validation rule enforced by the SpecKit system. It covers rule behavior, severity levels, detection patterns, and remediation steps for each validation check.

**Core Purpose**:
- **Rule Documentation** - Complete specifications for all validation checks
- **Fix Instructions** - Clear remediation steps when validation fails
- **Configuration Guide** - Environment variables and usage patterns

### Core Principle

> Validation ensures spec folders meet quality standards before claiming completion—preventing incomplete documentation from passing the Completion Verification Rule.

### Severity Levels

| Severity | Exit Code | Strict Mode | Description                       |
| -------- | --------- | ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| ERROR    | 2         | 2           | Validation failed, must fix       |

# Ripgrep Retrieval Conventions

The invocation contract for free-text retrieval over spec docs and skill docs, replacing `memory_search`, `memory_context` and `memory_quick_search`.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Core Principle

Ripgrep is an evidence producer, never the relevance ranker. It returns matches, paths and lines. The caller decides what any of it is worth.

### The Two Lanes

Retrieval splits into a keyed lane and a free-text lane, and the two share no retrieval mechanism; they share the normalization and ranking helpers section 5 names.

| Lane | Mechanism | Used for |
|------|-----------|----------|
| **Gate 1 trigger lookup** | The generated index at `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/data/trigger-index.json`, read by `node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs "<prompt>"` | Matching a prompt against author-declared `trigger_phrases` |
| **Free-text evidence** | The ripgrep recipes in Section 2 | Finding a phrase anywhere in the corpus, with no index at all |

The two answer different questions. Prompt-to-declared-phrase matching is a keyed lookup over an author-controlled field. Grepping prose is a scan. Neither ranks by meaning: a phrase that no document spells literally is a clean no-hit, never a nearest guess.

# v2.12.2.0, Two CI Gates Go Green on Main

Two CI gates failed on main after the weak-model authoring work landed: changed-packet validation graded benchmark copies kept under `scratch/`, and the routing divergence ratchet saw `/deep:research :auto` prompts go to spec-kit. This patch fixes both at the source and clears the docs findings from the same audit.

> Spec folder: `specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/021-ci-gate-regressions` (Level 2)

 

## What's New at a Glance

- **Changed-packet validation skips `scratch/`.** A `spec.md` under a packet's `scratch/` folder is evidence, not a packet, so the gate no longer grades it, as the validator's own discovery never has. A packet whose name only contains the word scratch is still graded.
- **`/deep:research :auto` routes to deep-loop again.** The advisor phrase `draft auto-repair` gave spec-kit the token `auto`; it is now `spec docs`, and the compiled skill graph is rebuilt.
- **The authoring card passes the document validator.** It gained section separators and an `OVERVIEW AND BOUNDS` heading, with no wording change to any step.
- **Level docs call `decision-record.md` a lazy add-on.** The validation rules, the path-scoped rules, the level guide and `validate.sh --help` match what a Level 3 scaffold creates.
- **Lint stops counting build output.** ESLint ignores every `dist/` folder, not only the top-level one.

 

## Upgrade

No migration required. No validation rule changed, so every packet keeps its verdict. A prompt that names Draft auto-repair without naming the spec packet may now rank another skill first.
